grammar.label: the perfect progressive as evidence — it has been raining
grammar.form: have / has / had been + -ing, used to explain a present or past state
grammar.meaning: points at a finished activity to explain a visible result

explanation.en: 'The road is wet — it has been raining.' The perfect progressive is not only about duration; it is how English reasons backwards from a state to the activity that produced it. 'He had been drinking' explains a manner, not a length of time. That inferential use, rather than the durational one, is what C1 adds.
explanation.uz: 'The road is wet — it has been raining.' Perfect progressive faqat davomiylik emas: bu holatdan uni keltirib chiqargan harakatga qaytish usuli.

grammar.positive_example: Her hands were shaking; she had been carrying the boxes since six.
grammar.negative_example: Her hands were shaking; she carried the boxes since six.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida bunday xulosa chiqarish ko'pincha alohida gap bilan beriladi; ingliz tilida u zamon shaklining o'zida.

grammar.label: retrospective and prospective aspect — the futurate and the future perfect
grammar.form: will have + past participle; is to + base verb; was about to; is due to
grammar.meaning: places a viewpoint inside the future and looks back or forward from it

explanation.en: 'By March the inquiry will have sat for two years' puts the reader in March and looks back. 'The minister is to visit on Friday' is a scheduled future in formal register. 'Was about to' and 'was due to' put that viewpoint in the past. C1 is the level at which the viewpoint, not just the time, becomes something the writer chooses.
explanation.uz: 'By March the inquiry will have sat for two years' — o'quvchini martga olib boradi va orqaga qaraydi. C1 darajada yozuvchi nafaqat vaqtni, balki qarash nuqtasini ham tanlaydi.

grammar.positive_example: By the time the report appears, the committee will have been replaced twice.
grammar.negative_example: By the time the report appears, the committee is replaced twice.

l1_notes.uz: Kelasi zamonda perfekt tushunchasi o'zbek tilida kam uchraydi; vaqt nuqtasi so'z bilan beriladi.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: The lower field is under water again.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It has been raining since Thursday.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: It rains every autumn. The field has only flooded twice in forty years.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: So it is not the rain.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: It is not only the rain. Silt has been building up in the channel since they took the trees out above it.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That is a slow cause and a sudden result.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Most of them are. Nobody notices accretion until the day it matters.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: How do I write that without claiming more than we know?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: You tell them what you can see and let them ask why.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'The channel has been narrowing since 1998. The field has flooded twice, both times in the last four years.'

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: That will do. You have not said the one caused the other.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: By next spring the channel will have been narrowing for thirty years.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: And by next spring I will have been retired for two months, so you may put my name to it.
